posts.title: Renegade Cut - Thanos: Eugenics and overpopulation
posts.description:
Thanos's plan to erase half of all life mirrors eugenic ideologies, where elites justify mass harm by claiming it serves the "greater good."
It reflects a dangerous logic: that balance or progress requires sacrificing lives deemed less valuable.

posts.title: Philosophy Coded - Why stupid people is elected
posts.description: Why stupid people is elected

posts.title: Philosophize This - Michael Focault
posts.description:
What if control isn't about chains, but habits?
What happens when power doesn't punish, but molds us to behave?
Surveillance, standards, and constant evaluation keep us performing in society's never-ending test.

posts.title: PutoMikel - Buenos amigos
posts.description:
El género y la sexualidad no son fijos: lo que entendemos como normal hoy, puede haber sido muy distinto en otras épocas de la humanidad.
La heterosexualidad se asume como eterna y universal, mientras que la diversidad se considera moderna o "forzada".

posts.title: Story of Stuff - Story of Stuff
posts.description:
Still a gem, Story of Stuff (2007) mixes playful animation with sharp critique, revealing how production and consumption drive waste and inequality.
Its message: ditch the myth of linear economy and build systems that protect ecosystems.

posts.title: Carlos Maza - How media protect police
posts.description:
From Rodney King to George Floyd, cameras captured violence. Yet headlines reduced it to "clashes" or "incidents."
Carlos Maza shows exactly how the media's language shields violence and brutality.
Who knows? this might happen in your current timeline as well.

posts.title: Great Art explained in 15 minutes - Great wave of Hokusai
posts.description:
You know this, right? if so: why?
The video explores Japan's Edo-period, revealing how rapidly urban growth and rising merchant class gave Hokusai's access to vibrant colors and mass production prints, making the great wave a cultural phenomenon in countless homes.

posts.title: Rory Oneill - Panti's Noble Call
posts.description:
The 2014 Noble Call by Panti Bliss shaked the world.
Her phrase "that feels oppressive" captured a feeling shared by anyone who had ever been part of a minority. It became historic instantly, showing how personal truth can cut across borders and empower diverse communities.

posts.title: Boe Hoerman - The aesthetics of Fascism
posts.description: The aesthetics of Fascism

posts.title: Ted Talk - Sherry Turkle: Connected but Alone
posts.description:
Technological devices let us control and edit our interactions, avoiding awkwardness or spontaneity.
Real human connection requires openness, unpredictability, and vulnerability. Without them, every conversation can end up feeling like a polished performance.

posts.title: Atlas Pro - 7 continents of biogeography
posts.description:
Humans name lands after culture, history, and in some special cases based on their egos.
The video explores how drift, isolation and evolution created realms with unique biomes and species, reminding us nature defines boundaries far beyond our PETITE SMALL tiny political brains.

posts.title: Solar Sands - Reality isnt always right
posts.description:
Think of art, or even food ads, like storytelling with visuals: even when it looks realistic, the artist has chosen what to show, what to leave out and how to frame it.
That means it can guide how you feel or think. this is not a bad thing, but only important to notice when it happens.

posts.title: LonerBox - What is a woman
posts.description:
The definition of "woman" has real consequences for safety, rights and dignity. Narrow definitions risk excluding those wo do not fit strict biological criteria (like chromosomes) leading to stigma, discrimination and harm.
Definitions matter because legal policy, social recognition, and rights often depend on them.

posts.title: Not Just Bikes - Why cities are broke
posts.description:
Cities pay for old roads and services with money from new development, like paying one credit card with another.
It works only while growth continues; but when expanding the city slows down, the bills pile up.
Cities must reinvest in existing areas and build smarter, not just grow for the sake of growing.

posts.title: What I've Learned - Exercise and the brain
posts.description:
Every time you move, your brain makes new connections, like building roads between brain cities.
AND WELL, The more roads you have, the faster your brain can solve problems, focus better, handle stress, and maybe even be a little less of grumpy genius.

posts.title: Zach Star - How easy is to lie with statistics
posts.description:
The video uncovers classic data traps: like believing one thing causes another just because they happen together, or falling for sneaky graphs that distort information.
It encourages you to question numbers instead of just accepting them.

posts.title: Rationality Rules - When You Should LOSE an Argument on Purpose
posts.description:
I loved this video. You all know that Jubilee debate with Mehdi Hasan, right? This is easily the best breakdown of it.
It shows how he exposes hypocrisy, stays calm under pressure, and stands firm with courage. The brilliance is NOT about winning: it’s about dismantling stupidity.

posts.title: Daniel Matamala - Giro a la ultra derecha
posts.description:
Más allá de golpes de estado, la ultra-derecha (far right) debilita la democracia de forma lenta: intervienen el poder judicial, fiscalías, gobiernan por decreto y reduce la independencia de las instituciones.
Con ejemplos actuales, la entrevista es ideal si  sienten que la política es dificil de entender.

posts.title: Ted Talk - Eli Pariser - Filter Bubble
posts.description:
(2011) OLD BUT GOLD: The internet shows us info that matches our tastes and habits.
Because of that, we miss different opinions, important news, and ideas that challenge us.
This helps explain how people can end up with narrower or distorted views without even noticing.

posts.title: New Economic Thinking - How Economists Invented Austerity & Paved the Way to Fascism
posts.description:
Austerity wasn't about budgets. It was a way to push peoople back into dependence on bosses and old hierarchies.
 By making life harder and cutting public support, it weakened workers's ability to fight for change, showing how ecomonic rules can quielty shape power and control

posts.title: That Art History Girl - A history of feminist Art
posts.description:
Feminist art wasn't just about making new images, it was about fighting the world that tried to define women for them.
I like how this video brings the icons and rebels who used performance, craft, and raw honesty to expose the inequalities everyone else tried to ignore.

posts.title: Money & Macro - How the Nazis created an economic miracle
posts.description:
It shows how debt, repression and militarization fake prosperity, why such systems rely on permanent crisis or war to survive.
Simple look at those "state of emergency" and constant crisis reminders usually end up in models that implode, and never reflect true social or national well-being.
